I have added the following packages with the use of pacman ### Figure 3.13

Here you will make your figure. You can write a commit for each figure or error leading up to the figure that matches. Be sure to include commits of the transitions and name the figures such as “Recreating Figure 3.4” and “Recreating Figure 3.7”. Practicing frequent commits is a great habit.

gapminder_unfiltered

p <- ggplot(data = gapminder,
            mapping = aes(x = gdpPercap, y = lifeExp))
p + geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    scale_x_log10(labels = scales::dollar) +labs(x = "GDP Per Capita", y = "Life Expectancy in Years",
    title = "Economic Growth and Life Expectancy",
    subtitle = "Data points are country-years",
    caption = "Source: Gapminder.")
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

Figure 3.16

Here you will make your next figure.

p <- ggplot(data = gapminder,
            mapping = aes(x = gdpPercap, y = lifeExp))
p + geom_point(mapping = aes(color = continent,fill = continent)) +
    geom_smooth(method = "loess") +
    scale_x_log10()
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

Orignal graph

Continue practicing by accessing an unfamiliar data set from another package. You can load a dataset of your choice to show you can build a graphic using ggplot layers. Here are some sample data sets https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/datasets/html/00Index.html

y <- CO2 view(y)

p <- ggplot(data = CO2, mapping = aes(x = conc , y= uptake))

p + geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
    geom_smooth(method = "loess") +
    scale_x_log10() +
    labs(x = "Ambient CO2 Concentration(mL/L)",
         y = "carbon dioxide uptake rates (μmol/m^2sec)",
         title = "CO2 Concentration and Uptake Rate",
         subtitle = "each of the data points are individual grass plants",
         caption = "Source: Potvin, Lechowicz, and Tardif (1990)")
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
